summary: 1966 Bitterroot NF lookout on a 10-foot concrete base with R-6 cab, staffed most summers; still standing and NHLR-registered 2022. Current access and rental unconfirmed.

facts.design: 10-foot concrete base with R-6 flat cab

events.note: Built in 1966 as a 10-foot concrete base with R-6 flat cab
Firelookout.com says it replaced Palisade Mountain lookout 2 miles southeast; NHLR says it may have. Year assumed to be the build year.
Robert Smith to man the lookout in July 1969, per a Ravalli Republic item quoted on montanalookouts.weebly.com
Dominic Point Fire threatened the lookout on July 25, 2010; lookout evacuated and saved by retardant drops (single source)
Registered April 12, 2022 as US 1539, MT 102; nominated by Kyle Stetler

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says the tower replaced the Palisade Mountain lookout; the NHLR says it may have. Story reports both without choosing.
NHLR gives 8,206 ft (2,501 m); firelookout.com gives 8209 ft. The record's 2501.2 m matches NHLR.
NHLR says staffed nearly every summer; firelookout.com says every summer. Story says most summers.

notes_for_editor: Current access and rental status are unconfirmed: no visitor or access notice found, and Willow Mountain does not appear in the FFLOA rental directory checked (a negative finding, so no quote). The 2010 fire account comes from one site (montanalookouts.weebly.com); a Wildfire Today snippet mentions retardant drops on Willow Point lookout but was not fetched. The brief's height_m 3.0 is the 10-foot concrete base only. The 1966 replacement year is assumed to be the build year. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 1969 and 2010 dates and the Ravalli County location now have their own evidence quotes; the retardant sentence was reworded.
